What

What Brush Clearing Involves

Brush clearing is selective vegetation removal — the crew takes out undergrowth, saplings, and invasive brush while leaving the mature trees and structure you want to keep. It's the opposite of full lot clearing: precise, retained-canopy work rather than a bare-earth clear. Every brush-clearing job starts with a free on-site walk and a written estimate before you commit.

The equipment is matched to the job: a skid steer with a brush-mower attachment handles ground-level vegetation; chainsaw work takes down larger saplings and small trees; a chipper processes brush on-site or hauls it off; and hand-clearing covers tight access or selective work close to plantings you're keeping. Chip piles can be left on the property for mulch at no extra cost, or hauled away — your call.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Owners Call Roubic

The brush-clearing scenarios Aaron walks most often across NE Ohio properties.

Fence-Line Overgrowth

Rural property lines choke with brush and saplings. Annual or biennial fence-line clearing keeps the line open and the fence accessible.

Pasture Reclamation

Overgrown agricultural land reverting to brush. Mechanical clearing brings the pasture back into usable, mowable condition.

Invasive Species Taking Over

Buckthorn, honeysuckle, and multiflora rose crowd out natives. Mechanical removal is the first step toward a native landscape.

Blocked Views & Sight Lines

Undergrowth swallowing a view or a driveway sightline — cleared selectively while the mature canopy you want stays put.

How

Roubic's 4-Step Brush-Clearing Process

Every job starts with a free 20-minute on-site walk. Four steps from your call to job complete. Full scope on the Land Clearing hub.

1

Site Assessment

Aaron walks your property and the access route. Documents density, structure proximity, and what stays vs. goes.

2

Method Selection

We pick the approach that fits — skid-steer brush mower, chainsaw, chipper, or hand-clearing near plantings.

3

Clear + Cleanup

Brush cleared, chipped on-site or hauled off, ground raked clean. Retained trees left untouched.

4

Final Walk

Aaron or the lead walks the property with you to confirm it's clean. Itemized invoice emailed priority.

Common Brush Clearing Questions

Brush Clearing FAQ

Five things NE Ohio owners want to know before booking.

How much does brush clearing cost?
Brush clearing pricing typically runs quoted on-site depending on scope and density. Small fence-line jobs sit at the lower end; large pasture-reclamation projects at the upper end. Recurring service contracts qualify for package pricing. Every job is quoted on-site after a free walk.
Can Roubic remove invasive species?
Yes — mechanical removal of buckthorn, honeysuckle, multiflora rose, and other woody invasives is core Roubic work. We chip the vegetation on-site or haul it off. Long-term control may require herbicide follow-up by a licensed applicator, and we coordinate with applicators we trust.
Will you leave the wood chips for mulch?
Yes — many owners ask us to leave the chip piles for use as property mulch, and that's free. The standard option is full haul-off. Either way, there's no price difference.
Does brush clearing require a permit?
Generally no for selective brush clearing on private property. Large-scale clearing that approaches full lot-clearing scope may trigger village or county review — Roubic confirms whether anything is required during the free estimate.
Do you offer recurring fence-line clearing?
Yes. For rural properties with steady fence-line vegetation pressure, Roubic offers service contracts on annual or biennial cycles, coordinated with any selective tree work where overhanging canopy crosses the property line.
